samples.summary: New read-only gate on `YorkieStore.undo`/`redo` has no test; nothing pins the viewer-role refusal
samples.evidence: This delta adds `if (this.readOnly) return { success: false };` at yorkie-store.ts:1285 and :1291, described in its own comment as "the store is the enforcement point" for a viewer-role share visitor (the client-side half of the viewer-is-read-only property; the server half is the Yorkie auth webhook, packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts). Every `YorkieStore` constructed in a test is constructed writable — `new YorkieStore(doc, TabA)` (yorkie-store-undo.test.ts:41) and `new YorkieStore(doc, TabB)` (:155) — so no suite exercises the read-only branch of undo/redo at all. A future refactor that drops or inverts the gate (e.g. moving the check into `canUndo`, which is still ungated) fails no lane: frontend has no `tsc` and the vitest suite would stay green. Adding a case that builds `new YorkieStore(doc, TabA, true)`, seeds an undoable edit, and asserts `await store.undo()` is `{ success: false }` and that `doc.getRoot()` is unchanged would pin it. Not an exploit by itself — the webhook still refuses the `rw` PushPull — so the impact is a silently-reintroducible client-side gate plus a wedged viewer sync.

samples.summary: `canUndo`/`canRedo` were not given the same read-only gate as `undo`/`redo`
samples.evidence: The delta gates the two write paths (`undo` :1285, `redo` :1291) on `this.readOnly` but leaves `canUndo()` (:1370) and `canRedo()` (:1375) reporting the raw Yorkie history state. No current caller is exploitable: the share view's read-only mount hides the toolbar (`{!readOnly && (` at sheet-view.tsx:1630) and the engine refuses undo/redo before reaching the store (`if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;` at packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:650 and :664, plus the Cmd+Z/Cmd+Y key handlers at packages/sheets/src/view/worksheet.ts:5106 and :5120). So this is a consistency/hardening nit, not a bypass: a future read-only surface that enables an affordance from `canUndo()` would render it live even though the action is refused.

finding.summary: Rewritten `YorkieStore.undo()`/`redo()` omit the `this.readOnly` guard that every other CRDT-writing method in the class carries
finding.evidence: The class documents (constructor comment, yorkie-store.ts:91-107) that the read-only gate lives *in the store* precisely because "the engine's own `readOnly` bounds the editing commands, not the selection publish, so the gate has to be here" — a viewer-issued `doc.update()` is pushed with verb `rw`, which the Yorkie auth webhook refuses for a share-link `viewer`, wedging that viewer's sync. `updateSelection` (:661), `ensureAxisOrder` (:699) and the comment writes (:1381) all begin `if (this.readOnly) return;`. The rewritten `undo()` (:1276) and `redo()` (:1281) call `this.doc.history.undo()` — a `doc.update` — with no such check, and `replayHistory` additionally sets `this.dirty = true`. shared-document.tsx:347 states outright that "`readOnly` here is a UI decision, not the gate". Vector: any caller that reaches a read-only-constructed `YorkieStore` (sheet-view.tsx:1038 passes `readOnly` through) and invokes `store.undo()` produces an unauthorized write attempt from a viewer. I traced the two current callers — `Spreadsheet.undo()`/`redo()` (spreadsheet.ts:650,664) and the keyboard handler (worksheet.ts:5106,5120) — and both are `_readOnly`-gated, so I could not complete an exploit chain today; this is a missing defence-in-depth layer at the layer the codebase explicitly designated as the enforcement point, newly touched by this diff.

verdict.reason: The finding claims YorkieStore.undo()/redo() lack the `this.readOnly` guard that other CRDT-writing methods carry. The guard is present: yorkie-store.ts:1285 (`async undo()` -> `if (this.readOnly) return { success: false };`) and :1291 (`async redo()` -> same). Both checks execute before `canUndo()/canRedo()` and before `replayHistory()`, which is the only place the `doc.update()` write and `this.dirty = true` happen (:1272-1273). The doc comment at :1276-1283 explicitly states the store is the enforcement point and that the replay carries the same readOnly gate the constructor documents. A grep for `readOnly` in this file yields 661, 699, 1285, 1291, 1391 — the undo/redo pair is guarded exactly like updateSelection and the comment writes. Since the claimed missing defence-in-depth layer exists at the designated enforcement point, no viewer-role visitor can push an `rw` update via these methods, and the finding has no basis.
